The original four phases were independently validated against their task lists and quality gates.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:71:1. **Lane 1 — Claim-Adjudication Stop Gate Wiring** closed F002 and F007 by adding a universal STOP veto pre-check and a dedicated `claimAdjudicationGate` in the review legal-stop decision tree, plus persisted `claim_adjudication` events, typed packet docs in `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/state_format.md` §9, and matching `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/loop_protocol.md` §Step 4a. New REQs: REQ-026, REQ-027.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:72:2. **Lane 2 — Coverage-Graph Session Isolation** closed F004, F005, F006, and F013 by bumping `deep-loop-graph.sqlite` to v2 with a composite primary key of `(spec_folder, loop_type, session_id, id)` on both `coverage_nodes` and `coverage_edges`, migrating via drop-and-recreate, adding a shared-ID collisions regression to `session-isolation.vitest.ts`, and documenting the typed `graphEvents` payload shape and namespace rules in both state_format references. New REQs: REQ-028, REQ-029.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:75:5. **Lane 5 — Release-Readiness Reconciliation** closed F013, F014, F015, and F016 by rewriting the phase-008 closeout surfaces, the packet-root completion surfaces below, and the reducer-owned `ACTIVE RISKS` dashboard section so non-P0 release-readiness debt stays visible. New REQ: REQ-034.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:114:| Closing-audit Lane 1–5 remediation (REQ-026 through REQ-034) | PASS — see `008-further-deep-loop-improvements/implementation-summary.md` §Closing Audit Remediation Notes and `review/review-report.md` |\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:42:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D3: Is the mutation coverage graph namespace (`loop_type: \\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\"`) properly isolated from the deep-research/deep-review namespaces in the shared SQLite store?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:72:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D5: Does any loop phase (init / iteration / convergence / synthesis) actively READ from the coverage graph (`coverage-graph-query.ts`, `coverage-graph-convergence.cjs`) to inform decisions, or only WRITE to it?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:90:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D5: Does the coverage graph's contribution to the 3-signal convergence math exceed its weight, or is it merely nominal?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:301:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"`sk-improve-agent` follows a different path entirely: its resume contract replays a local \\\\\\\"coverage graph + registry\\\\\\\", and `mutation-coverage.cjs` persists an `improvement` JSON graph with `fs`/`path` helpers and `loopType: 'improvement'`, while the agent only consumes an orchestrator-provided summary as advisory context. That means it does not supply the missing shared `deep_loop_graph_*` bridge for research/review convergence (.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:9-10; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:21; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:50-67; .opencode/agents/agent-improver.md:175-177).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:319:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"Both deep-loop convergence contracts still document a reducer-owned in-memory graph bridge that is not present in the live reducer: deep research says \\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph\\\\\\\" when `graphEvents` exist, and deep review says the same for review iterations (.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205; .opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/convergence.md:658-683).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:711:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published deep-research contract says that when `graphEvents` exist, \\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph and derives additional signals for the legal-stop gate evaluation,\\\\\\\" including graph coverage sub-checks (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205`). The live research reducer does not implement that bridge: its only imports are `fs` and `path`, and its convergence score is taken from `latestIteration.convergenceSignals?.compositeStop` or `latestIteration?.newInfoRatio` rather than any graph helper (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:11-13`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:244-249`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1177:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The resume contract promises richer recovery than the shipped journal helpers provide. The skill says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the journal module only exposes raw-event readback, `getLastIteration()`, and `getSessionResult()`. If an interruption happens before a `session_ended` event is written, `getSessionResult()` returns `{ stopReason: null, sessionOutcome: null }`, so the helper surface itself does not reconstruct candidate, gate, benchmark, or trade-off state (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-300`, `.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:332-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:148-203`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1263:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published resume contract promises more reconstruction than the shipped recovery helper exposes. Both the command and skill say resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the only recovery-facing journal helpers return the max iteration number and the terminal `stopReason/sessionOutcome`; there is no helper that rebuilds blocked-stop payloads, trade-off state, benchmark warnings, or lineage context from raw journal events (`.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:334-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-295`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:168-203`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1530:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The shipped deep-review reducer mirrors the same pattern. `computeConvergenceScore()` reads `latest.convergenceSignals.compositeStop` or falls back to `1 - newFindingsRatio`, and the reducer then publishes only that scalar as `convergenceScore`. No inspected review reducer code reconstructs a coverage graph or invokes graph convergence logic before writing the dashboard/registry (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:360-390`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:579-583`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:671-680`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1551:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The standalone graph helper does have bounded weight, not runaway influence: `computeGraphConvergence()` builds `graphScore` from fragmentation (0.25), normalized depth (0.25), question coverage (0.30), and source diversity (0.20), then limits the merged result to `blendedScore = compositeStop * 0.6 + graphScore * 0.4`. Inside this helper, the coverage graph cannot contribute more than 40% of the final blended scalar (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/coverage-graph-convergence.cjs:141-205`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1735:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"A different namespace-isolation weakness does exist on the shared read side for research/review sessions: the convergence handler never accepts `sessionId`, constructs its namespace from only `{ specFolder, loopType }`, and then calls `getStats()` plus `computeSignals()` / `computeMomentum()` without session scoping, so convergence decisions aggregate all sessions sharing the same spec folder and loop type (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:47-52`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:92-111`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:511-545`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:163-220`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1779:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published `sk-improve-agent` contract and visible auto workflow keep that mutation coverage graph local to the improvement runtime rather than bridging it into the shared coverage-graph MCP. The skill describes `scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs` as the reader/writer for the coverage graph and says it uses `loop_type: \\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\"` isolation, while the auto workflow only appends the state ledger and runs `scripts/reduce-state.cjs`; I found no visible `deep_loop_graph_upsert` step on this path (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:298-300`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:389-390`, `.opencode/commands/deep/assets/improve_agent-improver_auto.yaml:149-155`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1801:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The query surface only partially exposes session isolation. `handleCoverageGraphQuery()` accepts `sessionId` and passes it into `ns`, but the inspected helper queries for coverage gaps, contradictions, and unverified claims read by `spec_folder` and `loop_type` only, ignoring `ns.sessionId`; this means research/review sessions can be co-mingled on read even though improvement-mode entries are blocked from the DB entirely (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:28-35`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:55-58`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:63-126`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:136-147`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:238-277`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1823:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The shared SQLite coverage graph does not admit `improvement` loop types at all. The DB layer defines `LoopType = 'research' | 'review'`, constrains valid kinds/relations by those two namespaces, and the schema enforces `CHECK(loop_type IN ('research', 'review'))`; the MCP upsert handler repeats the same validation and rejects any other value (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:17`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:136-146`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:152-157`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:51-53`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:72-80`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:2121:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"`SKILL.md` says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch and that the orchestrator skips mutation types already in the exhausted log, but the visible autonomous loop never invokes `mutation-coverage.cjs` before candidate generation. The shipped loop proceeds from integration scan directly to candidate generation, scoring, benchmarking, ledger append, reducer refresh, and reducer-driven stop check, so coverage state does not visibly steer mutation focus selection. (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300`, A `1/sqrt(neighbor_count)` fan-effect divisor (R17) prevents hub nodes from appearing in every co-activation result.\\n.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/search/README.md:662:The causal graph is condensed into strongly connected components, then longest-path depth is computed across the resulting DAG. Shortcut edges do not collapse deeper chains; cycle members share one bounded depth layer, and the final depth is normalized by the deepest reachable component chain (`maxDepth`). 5568:1. Finding ID: `F-004-001`
5573:Title: Session-scoped reads are inconsistent with the module’s own auto-created nodes
5574:Description: `insertEdge()` synthesizes missing nodes without any `sessionId`, but every session-aware reader/filter only trusts `node.sessionId` or `node.metadata.sessionId`. That means a caller can build a graph entirely through the public insert API, attach `metadata.sessionId` to edges, and still lose those nodes from `getNodes()` and any signal helper that depends on node-level session matching. This makes the session-aware export surface easy to misuse and hard to reason about.
5588:Recommendation: Centralize graph/session normalization in one shared helper and either propagate `metadata.sessionId` into synthesized nodes or add an explicit node upsert API. Add direct session-scoped tests for `getNodes()`, `getEdges()`, `getEdgesFrom()`, `getEdgesTo()`, and the signal helpers.
5590:2. Finding ID: `F-004-002`
5595:Title: `computeMomentum` has drifted away from the canonical runtime contract
5596:Description: The CJS helper exports `computeMomentum(graph, nodeId, windowSize, sessionId)` as a recent-edge counter, while the canonical runtime implementation exports `computeMomentum(specFolder, loopType)` as a snapshot-to-snapshot delta calculator in [.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:555). Same name, different meaning. That is a long-term drift trap for maintainers, especially because the requested test suite only validates the CJS behavior in [.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/tests/coverage-graph-signals.vitest.ts](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/tests/coverage-graph-signals.vitest.ts:117).
5614:Recommendation: Rename the CJS helper to something contract-specific like `computeRecentEdgeActivity`, or move both layers behind one shared abstraction with parity tests that explicitly guard expected differences.
5616:3. Finding ID: `F-004-003`
5621:Title: Cycle-handling contract is documented one way and implemented another
5622:Description: The depth routine claims cycles are handled by “capping at the number of nodes,” but the implementation actually assigns `0` to nodes that never reach zero in-degree. That is not a harmless comment mismatch: it makes cyclic nodes indistinguishable from roots and hides complexity from downstream consumers. The requested unit tests only cover DAGs and empty graphs, so this divergence is currently unguarded.
5630:Recommendation: Either implement the documented fallback for cyclic components or update the contract and add explicit cycle tests for `computeDepth()` and `computeAllDepths()`.
5632:4. Finding ID: `F-004-004`
5637:Title: The contradictions module’s higher-risk branches are only lightly covered
5638:Description: This module exposes session-aware scanning, enriched reporting, and density calculation, but the requested `coverage-graph-*.vitest.ts` suite never gives it the same direct coverage that `core`, `signals`, and `convergence` receive. In the requested files, `contradictionDensity()` is only asserted for the empty graph case, and there is no targeted check for session filtering, `byNode` grouping behavior, or evidence/reason propagation. That makes the export surface harder to refactor safely.
5656:Recommendation: Add a dedicated `coverage-graph-contradictions.vitest.ts` or expand the existing suite with session-scoped contradiction graphs, non-empty `contradictionDensity()` assertions, and `reportContradictions()` enrichment checks.

// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/**
 * Compute momentum (change rate) between the latest and previous snapshots.
 */
export function computeMomentum(specFolder: string, loopType: LoopType): Record<string, number> | null {
  const d = getDb();
  const snapshots = d.prepare(`
    SELECT metrics FROM coverage_snapshots
    WHERE spec_folder = ? AND loop_type = ?
    ORDER BY iteration DESC LIMIT 2
  `).all(specFolder, loopType) as Array<{ metrics: string }>;

  if (snapshots.length < 2) return null;

  const latest = JSON.parse(snapshots[0].metrics) as Record<string, number>;
  const previous = JSON.parse(snapshots[1].metrics) as Record<string, number>;

  const momentum: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const key of Object.keys(latest)) {
    if (typeof latest[key] === 'number' && typeof previous[key] === 'number') {
      momentum[key] = latest[key] - previous[key];
    }
  }

  return momentum;
}

Description: `insertEdge()` synthesizes missing nodes without any `sessionId`, but every session-aware reader/filter only trusts `node.sessionId` or `node.metadata.sessionId`. That means a caller can build a graph entirely through the public insert API, attach `metadata.sessionId` to edges, and still lose those nodes from `getNodes()` and any signal helper that depends on node-level session matching. This makes the session-aware export surface easy to misuse and hard to reason about.
Evidence:
```js
if (!graph.nodes.has(source)) {
  graph.nodes.set(source, { id: source, createdAt: new Date().toISOString() });
}
...
sessionId: typeof metadata.sessionId === 'string' && metadata.sessionId ? metadata.sessionId : undefined,
```
```js
if (typeof node.sessionId === 'string' && node.sessionId) return node.sessionId;
...
if (matchesSession(graph, node, sessionId, 'node')) results.push(node);
```
Recommendation: Centralize graph/session normalization in one shared helper and either propagate `metadata.sessionId` into synthesized nodes or add an explicit node upsert API. Add direct session-scoped tests for `getNodes()`, `getEdges()`, `getEdgesFrom()`, `getEdgesTo()`, and the signal helpers.

    51	function makeDomains(count: number, opts: { diverse?: boolean } = {}): Array<{ domain: string; authority: number; cluster: string; topics: string[] }> {
    52	  const domains = [];
    53	  const clusters = opts.diverse ? Math.max(10, Math.floor(count / 5)) : 2;
    54	  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
    55	    const clusterIdx = i % clusters;
    56	    domains.push({
    57	      domain: `source${i}.example.com`,
    58	      authority: 0.3 + (i % 7) * 0.1,
    59	      cluster: `cluster-${clusterIdx}`,
    60	      topics: [`topic-${i % 4}`],
    61	    });
    62	  }
    63	  return domains;
    64	}

The original four phases were independently validated against their task lists and quality gates.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:71:1. **Lane 1 — Claim-Adjudication Stop Gate Wiring** closed F002 and F007 by adding a universal STOP veto pre-check and a dedicated `claimAdjudicationGate` in the review legal-stop decision tree, plus persisted `claim_adjudication` events, typed packet docs in `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/state_format.md` §9, and matching `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/loop_protocol.md` §Step 4a. New REQs: REQ-026, REQ-027.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:72:2. **Lane 2 — Coverage-Graph Session Isolation** closed F004, F005, F006, and F013 by bumping `deep-loop-graph.sqlite` to v2 with a composite primary key of `(spec_folder, loop_type, session_id, id)` on both `coverage_nodes` and `coverage_edges`, migrating via drop-and-recreate, adding a shared-ID collisions regression to `session-isolation.vitest.ts`, and documenting the typed `graphEvents` payload shape and namespace rules in both state_format references. New REQs: REQ-028, REQ-029.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:75:5. **Lane 5 — Release-Readiness Reconciliation** closed F013, F014, F015, and F016 by rewriting the phase-008 closeout surfaces, the packet-root completion surfaces below, and the reducer-owned `ACTIVE RISKS` dashboard section so non-P0 release-readiness debt stays visible. New REQ: REQ-034.\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/implementation-summary.md:114:| Closing-audit Lane 1–5 remediation (REQ-026 through REQ-034) | PASS — see `008-further-deep-loop-improvements/implementation-summary.md` §Closing Audit Remediation Notes and `review/review-report.md` |\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:42:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D3: Is the mutation coverage graph namespace (`loop_type: \\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\"`) properly isolated from the deep-research/deep-review namespaces in the shared SQLite store?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:72:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D5: Does any loop phase (init / iteration / convergence / synthesis) actively READ from the coverage graph (`coverage-graph-query.ts`, `coverage-graph-convergence.cjs`) to inform decisions, or only WRITE to it?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:90:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"D5: Does the coverage graph's contribution to the 3-signal convergence math exceed its weight, or is it merely nominal?\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:301:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"`sk-improve-agent` follows a different path entirely: its resume contract replays a local \\\\\\\"coverage graph + registry\\\\\\\", and `mutation-coverage.cjs` persists an `improvement` JSON graph with `fs`/`path` helpers and `loopType: 'improvement'`, while the agent only consumes an orchestrator-provided summary as advisory context. That means it does not supply the missing shared `deep_loop_graph_*` bridge for research/review convergence (.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:9-10; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:21; .opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs:50-67; .opencode/agents/agent-improver.md:175-177).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:319:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"Both deep-loop convergence contracts still document a reducer-owned in-memory graph bridge that is not present in the live reducer: deep research says \\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph\\\\\\\" when `graphEvents` exist, and deep review says the same for review iterations (.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205; .opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/references/convergence.md:658-683).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:711:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published deep-research contract says that when `graphEvents` exist, \\\\\\\"the reducer builds an in-memory coverage graph and derives additional signals for the legal-stop gate evaluation,\\\\\\\" including graph coverage sub-checks (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/references/convergence.md:1181-1205`). The live research reducer does not implement that bridge: its only imports are `fs` and `path`, and its convergence score is taken from `latestIteration.convergenceSignals?.compositeStop` or `latestIteration?.newInfoRatio` rather than any graph helper (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:11-13`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:244-249`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1177:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The resume contract promises richer recovery than the shipped journal helpers provide. The skill says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the journal module only exposes raw-event readback, `getLastIteration()`, and `getSessionResult()`. If an interruption happens before a `session_ended` event is written, `getSessionResult()` returns `{ stopReason: null, sessionOutcome: null }`, so the helper surface itself does not reconstruct candidate, gate, benchmark, or trade-off state (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-300`, `.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:332-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:148-203`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1263:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published resume contract promises more reconstruction than the shipped recovery helper exposes. Both the command and skill say resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch, but the only recovery-facing journal helpers return the max iteration number and the terminal `stopReason/sessionOutcome`; there is no helper that rebuilds blocked-stop payloads, trade-off state, benchmark warnings, or lineage context from raw journal events (`.opencode/commands/deep/start-agent-improvement-loop.md:334-339`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:290-295`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/scripts/improvement-journal.cjs:168-203`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1530:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The shipped deep-review reducer mirrors the same pattern. `computeConvergenceScore()` reads `latest.convergenceSignals.compositeStop` or falls back to `1 - newFindingsRatio`, and the reducer then publishes only that scalar as `convergenceScore`. No inspected review reducer code reconstructs a coverage graph or invokes graph convergence logic before writing the dashboard/registry (`.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:360-390`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:579-583`, `.opencode/skills/sk-deep-review/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:671-680`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1551:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The standalone graph helper does have bounded weight, not runaway influence: `computeGraphConvergence()` builds `graphScore` from fragmentation (0.25), normalized depth (0.25), question coverage (0.30), and source diversity (0.20), then limits the merged result to `blendedScore = compositeStop * 0.6 + graphScore * 0.4`. Inside this helper, the coverage graph cannot contribute more than 40% of the final blended scalar (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/coverage-graph-convergence.cjs:141-205`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1735:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"A different namespace-isolation weakness does exist on the shared read side for research/review sessions: the convergence handler never accepts `sessionId`, constructs its namespace from only `{ specFolder, loopType }`, and then calls `getStats()` plus `computeSignals()` / `computeMomentum()` without session scoping, so convergence decisions aggregate all sessions sharing the same spec folder and loop type (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:47-52`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/convergence.ts:92-111`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:511-545`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-signals.ts:163-220`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1779:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The published `sk-improve-agent` contract and visible auto workflow keep that mutation coverage graph local to the improvement runtime rather than bridging it into the shared coverage-graph MCP. The skill describes `scripts/mutation-coverage.cjs` as the reader/writer for the coverage graph and says it uses `loop_type: \\\\\\\"improvement\\\\\\\"` isolation, while the auto workflow only appends the state ledger and runs `scripts/reduce-state.cjs`; I found no visible `deep_loop_graph_upsert` step on this path (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:298-300`, `.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:389-390`, `.opencode/commands/deep/assets/improve_agent-improver_auto.yaml:149-155`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1801:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The query surface only partially exposes session isolation. `handleCoverageGraphQuery()` accepts `sessionId` and passes it into `ns`, but the inspected helper queries for coverage gaps, contradictions, and unverified claims read by `spec_folder` and `loop_type` only, ignoring `ns.sessionId`; this means research/review sessions can be co-mingled on read even though improvement-mode entries are blocked from the DB entirely (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:28-35`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/query.ts:55-58`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:63-126`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:136-147`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-query.ts:238-277`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:1823:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"The shared SQLite coverage graph does not admit `improvement` loop types at all. The DB layer defines `LoopType = 'research' | 'review'`, constrains valid kinds/relations by those two namespaces, and the schema enforces `CHECK(loop_type IN ('research', 'review'))`; the MCP upsert handler repeats the same validation and rejects any other value (`.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:17`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:136-146`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/lib/coverage-graph/coverage-graph-db.ts:152-157`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:51-53`, `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/coverage-graph/upsert.ts:72-80`).\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:2121:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"`SKILL.md` says resume replays the journal, coverage graph, and registry before dispatch and that the orchestrator skips mutation types already in the exhausted log, but the visible autonomous loop never invokes `mutation-coverage.cjs` before candidate generation. The shipped loop proceeds from integration scan directly to candidate generation, scoring, benchmarking, ledger append, reducer refresh, and reducer-driven stop check, so coverage state does not visibly steer mutation focus selection. (`.opencode/skills/sk-improve-agent/SKILL.md:294-300`, `.opencode/commands/deep/assets/improve_agent-improver_auto.yaml:137-158`)\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:2513:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"I did not find a shipped orchestrator implementation file that performs the promised “replay journal + coverage graph + registry before dispatch,” so this pass had to prove absence via reducer inputs and helper interfaces rather than a single end-to-end resume driver.\\\",\\n.opencode/specs/skilled-agent-orchestration/042-sk-deep-research-review-improvement-2/research/findings-registry.json:2558:      \\\"text\\\": \\\"A command-doc requirement to invoke I’ve finished the file-by-file validation pass and I’m tightening the findings into the final review format now. One remaining theme is that several fixes landed correctly, but a few maintainability issues are only partially resolved because the new APIs/helpers exist without being made canonical everywhere.
codex
**Findings**
- `F-024-001`
  Severity: `P1`
  Dimension: `maintainability`
  File: [wave-coordination-board.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/wave-coordination-board.cjs:96)
  Title: Board transition API exists, but the canonical board still does not advance its own status
  Description: The fix batch added `transitionBoardStatus()`, but `createBoard()` still initializes `status` once and `updateBoard()` never mutates it. In practice the board can keep rendering stale lifecycle state unless another caller explicitly wires the new API in.
  Evidence: `createBoard()` sets `status: 'initialized'` at line 96; `updateBoard()` only updates timestamps, segment state, findings, and stats at lines 131-176; `transitionBoardStatus()` exists separately at lines 331-372.
  Recommendation: Make board status transitions canonical by routing lifecycle updates through `transitionBoardStatus()` or by deriving board status inside `updateBoard()`.

- `F-024-002`
  Severity: `P1`
  Dimension: `maintainability`
  File: [wave-lifecycle.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/wave-lifecycle.cjs:248), [wave-coordination-board.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/wave-coordination-board.cjs:236), [wave-segment-state.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/wave-segment-state.cjs:185)
  Title: Merge behavior still diverges across lifecycle, board, and segment-state helpers
  Description: The board now uses the intended 5-key composite dedupe, but lifecycle joining and segment-state merging still apply different keys and conflict rules. The fix removed one hotspot, not the three-way divergence that made the merge contract hard to reason about.
  Evidence: Board merge now keys on `(sessionId,generation,segment,wave,findingId)` at lines 236-243 and 513-533; lifecycle join still uses `buildFindingKey()` based on `sessionId:generation:findingId` at lines 248-329 and 417-424; segment-state merge still falls back to `file:line::title` via `buildMergeKey()` at lines 185-278 and 370-375.
  Recommendation: Define one canonical merge contract and make the lifecycle and segment-state layers consume it instead of maintaining separate dedupe logic.

- `F-024-003`
  Severity: `P2`
  Dimension: `maintainability`
  File: [coverage-graph-signals.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/coverage-graph-signals.cjs:146)
  Title: Public alias keeps the old `computeMomentum` name drift alive
  Description: The new `computeRecentEdgeActivity()` function is present, but `computeMomentum` is still exported as a public alias. That improves compatibility, but it does not fully close the naming drift that the earlier review flagged.
  Evidence: `computeRecentEdgeActivity()` is defined at lines 146-168, `const computeMomentum = computeRecentEdgeActivity` is declared at line 170, and both names remain exported at lines 396-402.
  Recommendation: Deprecate and remove the alias after downstream migration, or document the alias as the permanent compatibility contract.

- `F-024-004`
  Severity: `P2`
  Dimension: `maintainability`
  File: [coverage-graph-session.cjs](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/coverage-graph-session.cjs:56)
  Title: Mixed-session edges now resolve by undocumented target-node precedence
  Description: The new centralized session helper improves consistency, but when an edge has no explicit session and its endpoints disagree, the helper silently assigns the edge to the target node’s session. That asymmetry is not obvious from the API and makes the normalization rule harder to reason about.
  Evidence: `getEdgeSessionId()` checks explicit edge metadata first, then source node session, then target node session, with the final fallback at lines 56-59.
  Recommendation: Reject mixed-session edges without explicit `edge.sessionId`, or document and test the precedence rule explicitly.

**Original Finding Status**

  Title: Board transition API exists, but the canonical board still does not advance its own status
  Description: The fix batch added `transitionBoardStatus()`, but `createBoard()` still initializes `status` once and `updateBoard()` never mutates it. In practice the board can keep rendering stale lifecycle state unless another caller explicitly wires the new API in.
  Evidence: `createBoard()` sets `status: 'initialized'` at line 96; `updateBoard()` only updates timestamps, segment state, findings, and stats at lines 131-176; `transitionBoardStatus()` exists separately at lines 331-372.
  Recommendation: Make board status transitions canonical by routing lifecycle updates through `transitionBoardStatus()` or by deriving board status inside `updateBoard()`.
